notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (MarinaIQ) building AI-first conversational support assistant. Initially want Hosted API for fast time-to-value; evaluating Dedicated if cost or data residency requires. Primary driver: low-latency streaming with reliable tool-calling (search + ticket-creation).

Key ask from PM/Eng: 'we need first token streaming start <200ms p50 under 20 concurrent agents' — realistic SLO target. Also want deterministic fallbacks when capacity constrained (model routing). Cost sensitivity: want guidance on batching/caching to keep token cost below internal target (~$0.02/conversation on average).

Security: strong mid-market checklist. Must have SSO/SAML for admin console, SOC2 attestation for hosted, audit logs (token-level obfuscation), KMS for customer-managed keys optional, and clear policy for PII redaction in request logs. Legal asked: can Redwood provide redaction hooks or automatic PII masking before persistence? They flagged retention_controls and data_residency for EU customers.

POC plan:
- Phase 1 (hosted): integrate Redwood SDK -> implement streaming chat + tool-calls to search/ticket API. Measure start-of-stream latency, token p50/p95, and tail latencies, and collect memory of KV cache hit rates.
- Phase 2 (scale): simulate 20–100 concurrent agents, run 3-day soak to measure cost and latency.
- Phase 3 (decision): evaluate Dedicated pricing if hosted costs exceed forecast or if VPC/residency required.

Sales/Legal notes: Sent security questionnaire 2026-03-02; awaiting SOC2 artifact (hosted) and clarification on log retention window. Price sensitive — procurement wants cap on Dedicated over first 12 months.

Quote from CPO on call 2026-02-20: 'We need streaming to feel instant for customers — missing that will kill adoption.'

Misc: Fireflies transcripts attached; internal eng notes in Drive. Jira INFRA-3217 opened for engineering question on tool-caller TLS mutual auth.
